q-114875.name: Question 1
q-114875.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3{x}^{2})(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2})(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}-3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,dx \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+D\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}-3\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}-3(-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+D) \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-3D.$ Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{3{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )}{2}+\frac{3(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )}{4}-(\frac{3(0)^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)}{2}+\frac{3(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)}{4}) \\  & =0+\frac{3\pi (-1)}{4}-0-0 \\  & =-\frac{3\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

q-114875.html:
Question 1
?

Evaluate the integral ∫0π/23x2cos⁡(2x)dx.

a
 3π2
b
 −π4
c
 −π2
d
 π4
e
 −3π4
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define u=3x2⟹dudx=6xdvdx=cos⁡(2x)⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫cos⁡(2x)dx=sin⁡(2x)2.

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get ∫3x2cos⁡(2x)dx=∫udxdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(3x2)(sin⁡(2x)2)−∫(sin⁡(2x)2)(6x)dx=3x2sin⁡(2x)2−3∫0π/2xsin⁡(2x)dx.

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate ∫xsin⁡(2x)dx. We take u=x⟹dudx=1,dvdx=sin⁡(2x)⟹v=∫sin⁡(2x)dx=−cos⁡(2x)2.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫xsin⁡(2x)dx=∫udxdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=x(−cos⁡(2x)2)−∫(−cos⁡(2x)2)⋅1dx=−xcos⁡(2x)2+12∫cos⁡(2x)dx=−xcos⁡(2x)2+sin⁡(2x)4+D where D is an integral constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is ∫3x2cos⁡(2x)dx=3x2sin⁡(2x)2−3∫xsin⁡(2x)dx=3x2sin⁡(2x)2−3(−xcos⁡(2x)2+sin⁡(2x)4+D)=3x2sin⁡(2x)2+3xcos⁡(2x)2−3sin⁡(2x)4+C

where C=−3D. Finally then, we can work out the definite integral: ∫0π/23x2cos⁡(2x)dx=[3x2sin⁡(2x)2+3xcos⁡(2x)2−3sin⁡(2x)4]0π/2=3(π2)2sin⁡(π)2+3(π2)cos⁡(π)2−3sin⁡(π)4−(3(0)2sin⁡(0)2+3(0)cos⁡(0)2−3sin⁡(0)4)=0+3π(−1)4−0−0=−3π4

q-114883.name: Question 2
q-114883.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3}))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})-6\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3}))(x)-\int (x)(\frac{3}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3\int \text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is a constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & =x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})-6(x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})-3x+D) \\  & =x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})-6x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})+18x+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-6D.$ 

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})\,\text{d}x & ={[x{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{3})-6x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{3})+18x]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =[e{ln}^{2}⁡({e}^{3})-6e\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3})+18e]-[(1){ln}^{2}⁡({1}^{3})-6(1)\operatorname{ln}⁡({1}^{3})+18(1)] \\  & =9e-18e+18e-18 \\  & =9e-18.\end{aligned}
$$

q-114883.html:
Question 2
?

Evaluate ∫1eln2⁡(x3)dx.

a
 9e−18
b
e−18
c
9e+12
d
3e+9
e
3e−9
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define u=ln2⁡(x3)⟹dudx=6ln⁡(x3)xdvdx=1⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫dx=x.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫ln2⁡(x3)dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(ln2⁡(x3))(x)−∫(x)(6ln⁡(x3)x)dx=xln2⁡(x3)−6∫ln⁡(x3)dx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫ln⁡(x3)dx. We take

u=ln⁡(x3)⟹dudx=3xdvdx=1⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫dx=x.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫ln⁡(x3)dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(ln⁡(x3))(x)−∫(x)(3x)dx=xln⁡(x3)−3∫dx=xln⁡(x3)−3x+D, where D is a constant.

So, we get that the indefinite integral is ∫ln2⁡(x3)dx=xln2⁡(x3)−6(xln⁡(x3)−3x+D)=xln2⁡(x3)−6xln⁡(x3)+18x+C, where C=−6D.

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral: ∫1eln2⁡(x3)dx=[xln2⁡(x3)−6xln⁡(x3)+18x]1e=[eln2⁡(e3)−6eln⁡(e3)+18e]−[(1)ln2⁡(13)−6(1)ln⁡(13)+18(1)]=9e−18e+18e−18=9e−18.

q-346501.name: Question 3
q-346501.worked_solution:
We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2} & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=18{x}^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int 18{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=6{x}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 18{x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}(6{x}^{3})-\int (6{x}^{3})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =6{x}^{3}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{2}-12\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate $\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={x}^{2} & \,⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡x(\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})-\int (\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})(\frac{1}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$

q-352028.name: Question 4
q-352028.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=27{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=54x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 27{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(27{x}^{2})(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})(54x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+18\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 27{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+18\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+18(\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{9}+D) \\  & =-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=18D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}27{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={[-9{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)+6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)]}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =9{(\frac{\pi }{3})}^{2}-2-2 \\  & ={\pi }^{2}-4 \\  & ={\pi }^{2}-4\end{aligned}
$$

q-352118.name: Question 5
q-352118.worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3{x}^{2})(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,dx \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6(-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+D) \\  & =3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-6D.$

Finally, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & ={[3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(3(\pi )^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+6(\pi )\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))-(3(0)^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+6(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =0+6\pi (-1)-0-0 \\  & =-6\pi \end{aligned}
$$
